description.en: Chosen design for future canonical Integer namespace forwarding, with exact loading, binding, error-carrier and verification boundaries.
description.ko: 향후 기본 Integer 네임스페이스 전달에 사용할 설계와 모듈 로딩, 이름 결합, 오류 전달 타입 및 검증 경계를 구분한다.

current_implemented.public_access: Explicit import integer, followed by integer.checked_add and other documented source calls.
current_implemented.error_carrier: integer.IntegerArithmeticError implements Copy, Error: Overflow and DivisionByZero.
current_implemented.canonical_integer_conversion: Existing Integer.convert remains a compiler-native conversion returning the existing IntegerError.OutOfRange carrier.
current_implemented.not_implemented: Canonical forwarding for the new source functions is not enabled. No source declaration can redeclare the prelude Integer type.

provider_loading: Resolve the ordinary user module graph and original AST names first.
Collect only call nodes whose receiver resolves to the exact declaration-free prelude Integer symbol and whose method is in a closed, shared forwarding registry.
Skip existing native conversion operations, unsupported names, ordinary user members, shadowed names and imports with matching spelling.
Add the standard integer provider once through its compiler installation path, not through project module search or arbitrary module roots. Preserve exact standard-module provenance and ModuleId.
Do not add ordinary source-visible import names or wildcard access. Provider top-level initialization must remain free of mutable persist values and side effects for implicit builtin use.
Resolve the expanded graph without changing the original builtin identity. Programs with no forwarded calls, unused spellings or only Integer.convert must not parse or load this provider.
call_rewriting: Select exact public function declarations from the trusted provider and lower through existing ordinary overload selection, argument evaluation, borrowing, ownership and effect checks.
Existing GenericResolver builtinMember, originalReferences, compilerImport and use mechanisms are useful foundations, but a textual qualified-name replacement alone is insufficient.

The initial user-name pass must reject private, unimported and transitive source references before compiler imports are generated. Compiler-only references must not grant additional rights to unrelated user AST nodes.
Preserve generic clone provenance, named argument order, receiver permissions, exact overload type matching and diagnostics at the original call site.
One registry must drive provider demand, supported forwarding, signatures and generated API inventory. A method absent from the registry remains unsupported.

error_carrier.current_difference: Directly forwarding checked helpers would return integer.IntegerArithmeticError instead of the catalog's canonical IntegerError. This is a nominal type difference, not just a diagnostic wording difference.
error_carrier.chosen_boundary: Do not silently present source checked helpers as exact canonical catalog contracts.
possible_staged_implementation: Error-free arithmetic and bit functions can be considered first, with independent canonical spelling gates.
For checked functions, extend canonical IntegerError with appended Overflow and DivisionByZero only in a dedicated verified compiler batch, preserving the existing OutOfRange variant index.
Use an explicit, allocation-free adapter from provider Result errors to canonical IntegerError. Do not rely on structural enum similarity or implicit conversion.
Update every strict IntegerError shape verifier, constructor, CoreError adapter, exhaustive switch, diagnostic code and lifecycle record in the same batch.
error_carrier.implementation_status: The canonical error expansion and adapter are proposals for that future batch; neither is applied by this plan.

source_pointers.role: Standard installation-relative module loading and dependency graph registration.
Canonical builtin binding checks, generated declaration use and existing native conversion preservation.
Source import rights, compiler-only imports and type-operand hints; hints alone are not callable implementations.
Current module loading, initial name resolution and generic resolution sequencing.

required_gates: Original source tests continue to pass for explicit integer imports and native Integer.convert.
Every forwarded overload passes check, AOT O0/O2 and ORC JIT O0/O2 with the independent integer oracle, including signed MIN, zero divisors, huge exponents and exact return carriers.
User modules, imports, local bindings, structs and methods named Integer or integer do not acquire builtin dispatch by spelling.
Private helpers, selected imports, transitive imports and unrelated user references remain inaccessible after compiler imports are inserted.
Generic clones, forward declarations and recursive helper calls retain canonical binding provenance.
No forwarded use, convert-only use and unsupported method names do not load the standard integer provider or create new public names.
A missing provider file diagnoses only actual supported forwarded use; a project module cannot replace the standard provider.
Forwarding introduces no runtime namespace object, implicit clone, heap allocation or mutable initialization dependency.
Canonical error adaptation validates nominal enum identity and every error path independently from source-carrier success.
remaining_catalog_boundary: This plan does not add type-operand APIs, radix parsing, formatting, checked shifts, bit fields, wide arithmetic or other missing catalog operations. Each requires its own provider and exact contract tests.
